doc: The state machine of an update item (haynes.upgrade-item/v1 state) and the events that move it (haynes.upgrade-event/v1). An event is legal only as an edge here: its type, its from state (null = first event of the item), its to state, and an actor kind the edge allows. 'requires' names the event fields that type must carry (a path such as evidence.merge_commit; 'drill' means drill must be true). starts_attempt: the event opens attempt n+1. attempt_result / recovery: what the event sets on that attempt's entry in the item's attempts[]. Reference: .agents/reference/upgrade-records.md.

needed.meaning: An update is available and nothing is in flight. lane says who may act; piece 1's lane starts a merge only from here and only for lane A-night.

held.meaning: A deliberate hold applies (.renovate/holds.json5 or a current-head vet HOLD). Nobody acts until it lifts.

blocked.meaning: Something about the item must change first: a check failing or incomplete, facts incomplete, a merge refusal that needs a new head, or (story 753) a version remembered as reverted on a new carrier.

unknown.meaning: The item could not be read; coverage says why. Unknown beats guessing.

closed.meaning: No longer offered: the carrier closed without a merge or a newer version replaced it. A reopened carrier is observed again.

in_progress.meaning: The lane took the change lock and its merge step is running (story 752; lock phase taken, then merging). Ends in merged, merge-refused, merge-failed or merge-unknown.

merge_unknown.meaning: The merge call was made and its outcome could not be read: GitHub may have merged. The change lock keeps its hold (lock phase merge-unknown). Owed: read the PR; merged at that head is merged, open at that head is merge-failed, still unreadable past its time box is escalated.

merged_unverified.meaning: Merged; the rollout is not yet verified. Backfilled merges stay here: nobody verified them.

awaiting_pin.meaning: An own-image source merged; verification waits, time-boxed, for the digest pin to merge, apply and soak (story 553).

done.meaning: Merged and verified. Counts as done.

failed.meaning: Verification failed, or a drill asked for a revert; no revert is open yet.

reverting.meaning: A revert pull request is open and not merged (story 753).

reverted_unverified.meaning: The revert merged; recovery is not yet verified.

reverted.meaning: Reverted and recovery verified. Sticky: the version is never merged again; only drill-cleared (a drill) or resolved by a person leaves it. A new carrier for the version is classed BLOCKED 'reverted' by the lane and writes no event here.

escalated.meaning: The lane's own moves are used up (recovery failed, a revert cannot be opened or merged, verification cannot be read); a person owns it (story 554).

approved.meaning: Reserved for piece 2 (dev-env v2 approval framework). Refused in piece 1.

scheduled.meaning: Reserved for piece 2 (a planned time from schedule, e.g. Renovate's Awaiting Schedule items). Refused in piece 1.

reserved.why: Piece 1 reads no approval (saga 547 comment 6922) and plans no schedule. These names keep their meaning for piece 2; the validator refuses them until a reviewed change lifts the reservation.

lock_phases.doc: The phases night-merge.mjs writes to ConfigMap upgrade-agent/upgrade-change-lock (story 752), and the item state each one goes with. released (or a lapsed lease) means no merge call is in flight; until story 553 holds the lock through verification, a merged item outlives its post-merge lease. A tick that takes over an expired lock reads took_over_phase: taken means the call was never made (merge-refused, class attempt-abandoned); merging or merge-unknown means it may have been (read the PR: merged, merge-failed, or merge-unknown).

observed.meaning: The lane read the item and its verdict changed (first sight, or a new state, lane or class). An unchanged read writes no event; the item's observed_at moves.

closed.meaning: The carrier closed without a merge, or a newer version replaced it. actor is who closed it when known, else lane (the observer).

merge-attempted.meaning: The merge step started: lock taken, preflight running. Only from needed; the lane only for an item in lane A-night. A hand run (story 712) may record its own attempt for an update Tom agreed to by phone prompt.

merge-refused.meaning: The merge step refused before any merge call, with its reason in class and reason and, from the lane's merge step, its pr_refusals and lane_refusals in evidence (pending status, checks older than main, head behind main, lock held, pause set; or an attempt abandoned by a crashed tick whose lock was still in phase taken). On a revert, the revert's merge was refused and stays owed.

merge-failed.meaning: The merge call was made and did not merge: a real exit status with the PR still open at that head (verdict merge-failed), or a later read of a merge_unknown item finds it open at that head. The lock is released.

merge-unknown.meaning: The merge call was made and its outcome could not be read (verdict merge-unknown: no exit status, or the PR could not be read after the call). Also what a tick records when it takes over an expired lock left in phase merging and cannot read the PR.

merged.meaning: The carrier merged. From in_progress by the lane's own merge step (verdict merged), or from merge_unknown when a later read finds it merged at that head; from an open state when someone else merged it (Renovate auto-merge, the shepherd, a hand run, a person), which opens a new attempt; from null when the first sight of the item is its merge (a backfill).

awaiting-pin.meaning: An own-image source merged; the verifier waits for the digest pin (the lane's cluster_effect_wait).

verified.meaning: The read-only verifier proved the rollout healthy: revision applied, Kustomization and HelmReleases Ready, new tag or digest running, soak clean.

verification-failed.meaning: Verification failed; class is the failure mode (not-applied, not-ready, wrong-image, restart-growth, critical-alert, pin-timeout).

drill-requested.meaning: A drill request in git names this verified merge: the lane reverts it as if verification had failed. Opens its own attempt, marked drill.

revert-opened.meaning: A revert pull request was opened (the lane's is night/revert-<PR>, one commit that exactly reverts the merged squash commit).

revert-merged.meaning: The revert merged. From reverting for a revert pull request that was recorded as opened; from failed, merged_unverified, awaiting_pin or done for a revert made by a person or a hand run without that record (also how a backfill records a revert found by its title).

recovery-verified.meaning: After the revert, the verifier proved the target healthy again. The version is now remembered as reverted.

recovery-failed.meaning: After the revert the target is still unhealthy. The lane stops; a person owns it.

escalated.meaning: The lane cannot finish on its own: a merge outcome stays unreadable, a revert cannot be opened or merged within its time box, or verification cannot be read. A person owns it.

resolved.meaning: A person settled an item: an escalated one is healthy at the new version (done), back on the old one (reverted), or no longer applies (closed); a reverted one is released because the revert was not the version's fault (needed) or no longer applies (closed). Only a person releases a remembered version.

drill-cleared.meaning: The drill is over and its marker cleared: the version is not remembered as bad and may be merged again. Legal only when the item's current attempt is a drill.

approval-recorded.meaning: Reserved for piece 2: an approval from the dev-env v2 approval framework.

schedule-set.meaning: Reserved for piece 2: a planned time for the update.
